english: Let $n=9999$, and let $A=\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac{1}{\sqrt k+\sqrt{k+1}}$ and $B=\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac{1}{(k+1)\sqrt k+k\sqrt{k+1}}$. Then the value of $\log_{10}\left(\dfrac{B}{A}\right)$ is ______.
hindi: माना $n=9999$ है, तथा $A=\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac{1}{\sqrt k+\sqrt{k+1}}$ और $B=\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac{1}{(k+1)\sqrt k+k\sqrt{k+1}}$ है। तब $\log_{10}\left(\dfrac{B}{A}\right)$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $(k+1)\sqrt k+k\sqrt{k+1}=\sqrt k\sqrt{k+1}\left(\sqrt{k+1}+\sqrt k\right)$, so the term is $\dfrac{\sqrt{k+1}-\sqrt k}{\sqrt k\sqrt{k+1}}=\dfrac1{\sqrt k}-\dfrac1{\sqrt{k+1}}$
solution_full: Multiplying by the conjugate, $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt k+\sqrt{k+1}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{k+1}-\sqrt k}{(k+1)-k}=\sqrt{k+1}-\sqrt k$, so $A$ telescopes: $A=\sqrt{n+1}-1$.
For $B$, factor the denominator: $(k+1)\sqrt k+k\sqrt{k+1}=\sqrt k\sqrt{k+1}\left(\sqrt{k+1}+\sqrt k\right)$.
Hence the $k$-th term of $B$ is $\dfrac{\sqrt{k+1}-\sqrt k}{\sqrt k\sqrt{k+1}}=\dfrac1{\sqrt k}-\dfrac1{\sqrt{k+1}}$, and $B=1-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{n+1}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{n+1}-1}{\sqrt{n+1}}$.
originality_note: New: two surd telescopings of different shapes are compared; their ratio is exactly 1/sqrt(n+1) for every n, which the question exposes through a logarithm (way 5: surd rationalisation linked with a less familiar telescoping factorisation). Closest known: JEE Main 2012 'sum 1/(sqrt k + sqrt(k+1))' and the standard 'sum 1/((k+1)sqrt k + k sqrt(k+1))'. Different because: the asked quantity is their ratio, which cancels to 1/sqrt(n+1); each sum alone is a known ingredient.
blueprint_concepts: Telescoping series with surds in the denominator

concept_use.Miscellaneous telescopic series: B telescopes after factoring (k+1)sqrt k + k sqrt(k+1) = sqrt k sqrt(k+1)(sqrt(k+1) + sqrt k), giving 1/sqrt k - 1/sqrt(k+1).
concept_use.Telescoping series with surds in the den: A telescopes after rationalising 1/(sqrt k + sqrt(k+1)) = sqrt(k+1) - sqrt k (surds in the denominator).
